note: Projected VECTOR onto a subspace: Apostol's general orthogonal projection s of x onto a finite-dim subspace S (via orthonormal basis, s=sum(x,ei)ei) specializes to Strang's projection p of b onto the column space C(A) in R^n; p=A(A^T A)^{-1}A^T b is the same vector, the non-orthonormal-basis matrix apparatus being the concrete representation only.

Projection onto a LINE = projection onto a 1-dim subspace: Apostol's projection onto S and the per-basis-element projection (x,ei)ei specialize to Strang p=(a^T b/a^T a)a. Same projected vector; a506's unit-ei case is generalized by any a.

Same math object (projection of a vector onto a subspace/column space) presented under different types: Apostol states it as a concept/element (the projection s); Strang s500 gives it as a method/procedure (three steps to compute p). types: concept (a-side) vs method (s-side).
Projection onto a line rendered as a procedure: Apostol concept/element vs Strang s509 method (three steps to compute p onto the line). types: concept (a-side) vs method (s-side).

Coefficient of the projection: Apostol's Fourier coefficients (f,phi_k) are the orthonormal-basis instance; Strang's x-hat is the best (least-squares) coefficient, x-hat=a^T b/a^T a. x-hat is the MORE general coefficient (reduces to (x,ei) when the basis is orthonormal), so general_tok is the s-side. Reversed-generality reach plus concept-vs-notation type gap keep confidence moderate.
Orthogonal decomposition: Apostol x=s+s_perp specializes to Strang b=p+e (p and e add to b); the error vector e=b-p is the concrete orthogonal component s_perp in R^n.

Pythagorean/orthogonality property of the projection: Apostol ||x||^2=||s||^2+||s_perp||^2 with s_perp orthogonal to S specializes to Strang's line case error e=b-p perpendicular to a and ||p||^2+||e||^2=||b||^2.

Orthogonality of the error to the subspace: Apostol's general notion 'element orthogonal to subspace S' specializes to Strang's theorem that e=b-A(x-hat) is perpendicular to the column space. The further claim that e lies in the left nullspace N(A^T) is a concrete matrix-only artifact with no abstract counterpart.

Best-approximation / closest-point property of the projection: Apostol a527 is 'Example 1', a worked Fourier instance minimizing ||f-f_n|| over trig polynomials in S (function space, type concept); Strang's 'closest vector/point p' (s500 column space, s509 line) states the property generally in R^n (type method). Downgraded from strict-same: a527 is a specific instance, not identical in object/type/domain, so it is a special case of the general closest-point property (general_tok s500). LEAST-SURE call.
Definition of distance between two elements (norm of x-y) in a Euclidean space. Strang uses distance only implicitly (||b-p||) and defines no analogous distance object; no concrete counterpart.

Element of the (2n+1)-dim trig-polynomial subspace (the Fourier example's target subspace S). Strang's analogous target subspace (column space / line) is referenced only inside other objects, never as a standalone element-of-subspace definition; no clean concrete counterpart.

Projection MATRIX P=A(A^T A)^{-1}A^T onto the column space. Concrete matrix-operator artifact; Apostol treats the projection as an element, not an operator/matrix, so no abstract counterpart. Concrete-only.
Projection matrix as a symmetric idempotent operator (P^2=P, p=Pb). Matrix-operator artifact; abstract text has no projection operator/matrix. Concrete-only.
Rank-one projection matrix onto a line P=aa^T/a^T a. Matrix-operator artifact; concrete-only (no abstract counterpart).

A^T A invertible iff A has independent columns (and shares A's nullspace, square/symmetric/invertible). Matrix-algebra fact underpinning the concrete projection formula; no abstract counterpart. Concrete-only.
Projection matrix properties P^T=P and P^2=P (projecting a second time changes nothing). Matrix-operator artifact; concrete-only.
